entities.summary:
Alfonso de Santa María de Cartagena was a Jewish convert to Christianity, a Roman Catholic bishop, diplomat, historian and writer of Renaissance Spain.

Born in 1425 in Granada, Spain, to a Jewish family, Alfonso was converted to Christianity in 1430. He studied law at the University of Salamanca and later became a bishop in the Catholic Church. Alfonso served as a diplomat for the Catholic Monarchs, Charles V and Isabella I of Castile, and was appointed as the Bishop of Cartagena in 1455.

As a historian and writer, Alfonso authored several works, including a history of the Christian conquest of the Iberian Peninsula. He also wrote about the Jewish community in Spain and their experiences under Christian rule.

Alfonso de Santa María de Cartagena died on July 21, 1456, in Cartagena, Spain.

Alfonso's works had a significant impact on the understanding of the Iberian Peninsula's history, particularly in the context of the Catholic Monarchs' reign. His writings helped to shape the narrative of the Christian conquest of Spain and the role of the Jewish community in the region.

In the centuries following his death, Alfonso's works were rediscovered and reevaluated, contributing to a renewed interest in the history of the Iberian Peninsula during the Renaissance.

A lasting cultural footprint of Alfonso's legacy can be seen in the many historical documents and texts that he authored, which continue to be studied by scholars today.

The irony of Alfonso's life and work lies in the fact that, despite his conversion to Christianity, he remained deeply connected to his Jewish heritage and the community that he had left behind.
